title: TapeWeave
subtitle: Reusable behavior. Application-owned outcomes.
voice: An interaction should be easier to deliver than a collection of screenshots. TapeWeave turns a small behavior into a runnable package: something a creator can share, an application can consume, and a reviewer can check. Here is the working product.

title: 01 / CREATE A BEHAVIOR
subtitle: Charge first. Trigger next. The timing is explicit.
voice: I start with charge and release. Generate the work, charge once, then trigger. The lamp lights. Trigger again without recharging, and no effect is requested. The trace exposes the old state, inputs, next state, and request, instead of hiding the rule behind an animation.

title: 02 / DELIVER AND RESTORE
subtitle: A portable package carries rules, not someone else's score.
voice: The package contains the rule, its digest, and the receiving scene. I copy it into the receiving field and validate it. That starts a fresh session. After two actions, I refresh and restore the saved execution. Recovery recomputes the steps rather than trusting a displayed score.

title: 03 / REJECT A CORRUPTED PACKAGE
subtitle: Validation failure preserves the current work and progress.
voice: Now I alter the digest in a copy of the package. Import fails, and the current session stays unchanged. This is a content consistency check, not publisher authentication. Ordinary shared truth tables remain available as a fair comparison; we do not claim that circuits are automatically better.

title: 04 / ONE BEHAVIOR, TWO APPLICATIONS
subtitle: The rule requests an effect. Each application enforces its own resources.
voice: The same behavior also runs in two application examples. One reveals a story; the other issues a local commemorative stamp. Each has separate state and resources. An effective request cannot bypass the stamp inventory. Both examples are built by us; they are not presented as independent adoption.

title: 05 / REAL X LAYER EVIDENCE
subtitle: Historical deployment and two complete runs: 11 published transactions.
voice: There is also a real X Layer integration. An account abstraction wallet deployed the host through Create X, then opened and completed both four-step cards. Eleven published transactions cover deployment and both runs. The interface separates this historical evidence from a fresh public R P C read.

title: 06 / READ THE CHAIN AGAIN
subtitle: Live read: pinned host runtime, canonical block and session state.
voice: I read the charge card session from the public network. Its final result is two training points, one opened door, and one remaining key. The alternating card produces a different outcome. Reviewers can download the evidence and rerun the verifier. A read-only result does not prove a new signature.

title: 07 / EXPLICIT WALLET BOUNDARIES
subtitle: No automatic signing. No EOA disguised as an AA account.
voice: The web wallet flows require explicit confirmation. The account abstraction entry checks deployed account code and native call capabilities, preserves unknown requests, and verifies successful User Operation events. This recording does not stage a signature. Full independent User Operation simulation and real browser A A acceptance remain separate milestones.

title: TapeWeave / BUILD, DELIVER, VERIFY
subtitle: Working prototype • Open source • Reproducible evidence
voice: TapeWeave is a working interaction delivery prototype, not a marketplace or a universal automation engine. The next test is independent developer integration, measured against ordinary shared code. Try the live demo, inspect the source, and reproduce the mainnet evidence. Create a behavior once. Make its meaning clear wherever it runs.
